R1.derivation: Absorbing rate ln2 from state0 gives 3/4 at t=2 and 7/8 at t=3. Waiting changes the experiment. Equal B/Q alone is insufficient.

R2.derivation: Known law is a point mass. Multiply its exact rational table; its second moment is (3/4)^2, not the moment of any finite Dirichlet.

R3.derivation: Symmetric Beta gives (k+2)/(4(k+1)); Beta(1,k+1) has positive forbidden mass at every finite k, so infinite cost does not converge to zero.

R4.derivation: Set every Q_m=0; T15's independent integrated discrete path sum remains. This full reduction uses unknown B/Theta and requires stage1b.

R5.derivation: Softmax at gamma0 is uniform on the declared candidate set; adding wait changes 1/2 to 1/3. Actual old model bytes come from baseline, not this oracle.

T1.derivation: For each forced A=a the reference and posterior of X are delta_a; the fair mixture over selected controls is not the reference.

T10.derivation: Absorbing 0->1 law is 1-exp(-ln2*t); switch at 1 integrates only the second of two one-second intervals.

T11.derivation: One shared W=2: accumulate 1/2, then remaining 3/2 at speed 2.

T13.derivation: Use E[p^k]=prod_i(a+i)/(a+b+i) in .8 Beta(2,1)+.2 Beta(1,2); compare Beta(9/5,6/5), not an expected-count update.

T14.derivation: Unobserved Bernoulli trial has likelihood p+(1-p)=1; uniform prior remains, integral p^2 dp=1/3.

T15.derivation: Enumerate 128 initial/state paths. Each path mass is 1/2 times the product over B and Theta columns of n0!*n1!/(n0+n1+1)!.

T16.derivation: H=1s read/reset: terminal KL is ln2/0, cost=0, gamma=1. exp(-J) is 2:1. Additional H=2 tree independently enumerates all terminal registered vectors, then checks forward total against backward recursion.

T17.derivation: U fair; R=.25/.75; T_in=R+10<11. tau=11+Delta. For U=0, survival at 12 is (1/8+1/2)/2=5/16. All observed clock readings and report names are constant, so posterior equals same-kernel reference.

T18.derivation: U is auxiliary, state initially 0. R=.25+U, think=10/10.5; all T_in<12. Shared waiting gives Z0=(1/8+1/2)/2=5/16 at 13. Fixing only the U=0 half to early/late gives (1/8+5/16)/2=7/32 or (1/2+5/16)/2=13/32.

T19.derivation: Enumerate U=0,1: max(1,.25+2U) is 1 or 9/4, both before 3. Both send and reset to 1. Dropping late U=1 changes half the reference.

T2.derivation: Enumerate X=0,1 with weight 1/2; O1=X and A2=O1. Identity keeps the original fair reference; both fully observed paths have KL=ln2.

T20.derivation: Exact R=1+U and tau=R+1/4. Observed R=2 already identifies U=1. Controlled reference stays fair; dropping both likelihoods or conditioning the reference makes posterior and reference identical.

T21.derivation: Keep Delta=.25 for U=0, .75 for U=1. Survival mass is .5/8=1/16; compare to the independent T17 table: (1/16)ln(2/5)+(7/16)ln(14/11).

T22.derivation: not_before=9/4 is after fixed X=S(2), preserving fair X and forcing Z=1. Removing reservation makes early U=0 reset before 2, so reference X=1 becomes certain (or 3/4 with exponential response).

T23.derivation: At 2, V is fair: exp[-(4/3)ln2*(2-5/4)]=1/2. Waiting until 9/4 then independent reset makes four joint cells 1/4. V=0 gives ln2; reading Z gives ln4. Constant report retains ln2.

T24.derivation: Chi is a shared law, not an individual delay draw. Two deterministic candidate laws with equal priors are identified by exact, but have identical integer readings when both lie in one tick.

T25.derivation: Count unique physical applications of B, not observations: start-impulse/2 applies once at dispatch, including self transitions.

T3.derivation: Flip preserves fair prior; full report gives entropy ln2. C maps both states to 0, so posterior and controlled reference are delta_0.

T4.derivation: Independent resets give two/four equiprobable registered state vectors.

T5.derivation: Integrate uniform p: integral_0^1 2*p*ln(2*p) dp=ln2-1/2. Y=S' is deterministic given (p,S'), so joint information=H(Y)=ln2.

T6.derivation: Known constant state with uniform Theta uses the same integral as T5. A constant likelihood in B leaves its density unchanged, KL=0.

T7.derivation: Measure the fair state before C, or deterministic 0 after C. Completion is after the impulse, before the next choice; it adds no extra uncertainty.

T8.derivation: Multiply column-stochastic kernels in causal order, from initial state 0.

T9.derivation: P=exp(Q*1s), Q[1,0]=ln2, Q[0,0]=-ln2. Apply C and P in both orders from state 1; column is departure. This includes nonzero Q.
